name: Quick start: install summary → instruction
old:
The install summary says whether the plugin is active or whether to run `/reload-plugins`: an install
from the shell does not reach a session that is already open.
new:
An install from the shell does not reach a session that is already open: run `/reload-plugins` there, or
start a new one.

name: §5 read grant: TMPDIR fallback
old:
It reads anything you can read, and your system
  temp directory is the only thing it may write — enough for most test suites, not for browser tests.
new:
It reads anything you can read, and one temp
  directory is the only thing it may write — yours, or the plugin's own when your shell names none.
  Enough for most test suites, not for browser tests.

name: §5 worktree kept on failure
old:
- **Writes in a throwaway copy of the repository.** Made for it, and removed once what it did has been
  saved.
new:
- **Writes in a throwaway copy of the repository.** Made for it, removed once what it did has been
  saved, and kept for you to look at when the turn fails.

name: §5 warning: continuation
old: > on an empty diff. Commit first.
new:
> on an empty diff. Commit first. A continued agent keeps the copy it had: to show it new commits, start a
> fresh one.

name: §6 four places, locks, pruning
old:
On disk it uses three places:

- **your system temp directory** — each agent's prompt and output files, and whatever a read-only agent
  writes while it works.
- **`~/.claude/plugins/data/codex-delegate-nowely`** — answers, run records, write locks, and a Codex home
  of the plugin's own, so your own Codex plugins, skills and memories cannot steer a turn.
- **`~/.codex/sessions`**, your own Codex home — each turn's full transcript lands there, so a check on
  what really ran has something to read.

Answers and run records age out by count and by age; the private home and the write locks stay.
new:
On disk it uses four places:

- **your system temp directory** — each agent's prompt and output files, and whatever a read-only agent
  writes while it works.
- **`~/.claude/plugins/data/codex-delegate-nowely`** — answers, run records, reports, write locks, a Codex
  home of the plugin's own, so your own Codex plugins, skills and memories cannot steer a turn, and the
  scratch of agents started from a shell that names no temp directory.
- **`.claude/worktrees` inside your repository** — the throwaway copies, while a turn runs and after one
  fails.
- **`~/.codex/sessions`**, your own Codex home — each turn's full transcript lands there, so a check on
  what really ran has something to read.

Answers, run records and that scratch age out by count and by age. Reports, the private home and a failed
turn's copy stay until you remove them; `/codex-delegate:cleanup` lists what the plugin left. A write lock
lasts as long as its run.

name: §9 no superlative
old:
driving `codex app-server`, the only Codex interface
that takes rights per call and reports what ran.
new:
driving `codex app-server`, the Codex interface that
reports back both the rights it applied and what each command did.

name: clone route: drop cleanup from the loop
old: for s in seat orchestrate cleanup; do
new: for s in seat orchestrate; do

name: clone route: say cleanup needs the install
old:
modes lose the plugin's prefix here: `/seat`, not `/codex-delegate:seat`. Update the clone with
`git pull`.
new:
modes lose the plugin's prefix here: `/seat`, not `/codex-delegate:seat`; `/cleanup` runs only from the
plugin install. Update the clone with `git pull`.

name: troubleshooting rows 2 and 3
old:
| the run is refused before it starts | your Codex quota window is full | wait, or use a Claude subagent |
| a run dies mid-way in a large fan-out | out of memory — runs are killed, not queued | ask for fewer at once |
new:
| the run is refused before it starts | the report's `error` says why: a full Codex quota window, a held write lock, a report path already used, no state directory | read it; for quota, wait or use a Claude subagent |
| a run dies mid-way in a large fan-out | out of memory — runs are killed, not queued — or the idle cut, which the report names and offers to resume | ask for fewer at once; a cut run continues from where it stopped |
